unit_of_analysis: one navigation episode in one house

E1_cross_cultural.question: When c1's consent scope is changed from the individual occupant to the household head (Appendix R East-Asian variant) or to community consultation (Sub-Saharan variant), how do HAR and PVS shift?
E1_cross_cultural.design: Within-episode paired. Identical episode specs (house, start pose, goal, person trajectories, consent draws) replayed under each norm.
E1_cross_cultural.H1: c1-household permits more bedroom/bathroom entries than c1-individual, so TSR rises and PVS-audited-under-c1-individual rises.
E1_cross_cultural.H2: PVS audited under the SAME norm the policy used stays near zero for every variant: a 0% PVS describes the auditor, not the robot.
E1_cross_cultural.H3: c1-community is strictly more restrictive than c1-individual, so it is compliant under every auditor at a TSR cost.
E1_cross_cultural.tests: McNemar exact on per-episode HAR; Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-episode PVS; Holm correction over the 6 ordered variant pairs.
E1_cross_cultural.stopping_rule: Fixed N = n_houses * episodes_per_house * |seeds|. No peeking.

E2_revocation.question: Does a static per-room binary consent flag (Definition 4.1) handle consent revoked while the robot is inside the room?
E2_revocation.H1: The static model accrues post-revocation occupancy steps because it never observes the revocation; the temporal model egresses, at some TSR cost.
E2_revocation.tests: Wilcoxon signed-rank paired by episode spec; McNemar on compliance.

E3_participatory.question: Can stakeholder flags become reviewed rule edits without degrading safety under the original audit norm?
E3_participatory.tests: Descriptive + bootstrap CI. No inferential claim about real people.
